description: Evidence-based research decisions, not live-database changes. Numbering is inherited from sources.

crosswalks.basis: Both describe the first-generation Kahana, companion of Rav Asi, who studied with Rav without adopting his approach and later interacted with Rabbi Chiyya's sons in Eretz Israel.
Rabbi Chiyya the compiler/student of Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi. Hyman's Rabbi Chiyya entry explicitly distinguishes him from Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba.
Third-generation Amora and student of Rabbi Yochanan; distinguish from Rabbi Chiyya the elder. Sefaria's outgoing Wikipedia link to Rabbi Chiyya is an erroneous cross-identity link.
Both biographies identify the student of Rav who fled Babylonia and studied with Rabbi Yochanan; source numbering also agrees.
Both identify the student of Rav Yehudah and Rabbah, companion of Rav Safra, student of Rabbi Abbahu, academy head at Pum Nahara and teacher of Rav Ashi.
Both distinguish the later Rav Kahana, contemporary of Rav Ashi and head of Pumbedita. Preserve their different generation labels; do not merge him with the Pum Nahara teacher of Rav Ashi.

rejected_external_links.reason: Biographies describe different teachers and generations; Hyman explicitly distinguishes the two.

manual_review.reason: Kahana, teacher of Rav, is a distinct Bonayich record; Wikipedia's first Kahana biography also describes Rav learning traditions from him. Determine whether this is an additional person or an alternative traditional identification before counting it separately.

assignment_exclusions.reason: Hebrew Wikipedia distinguishes Rabbi Yannai the Tanna, speaker in Avot, from Rabbi Yannai the Amora. Do not use the bare shared name or an upstream NER assignment to collapse them.

non_merge_examples.reason: Hyman's see-entry cross-reference can point to a joint discussion; it is not an assertion that the two names are one person.
Separate source-defined biographies, generations and interaction contexts. Generic כהנא mentions are not distributed to all four as proof of identity.
